helpIntro: USC uses a 4.0 scale with plus/minus grades from A through D-. Enter USC semester units and final grades to estimate your current, cumulative, projected, or target GPA.
helpNote: For the standard USC undergraduate institutional GPA. A+ is not used. F, UW, and IX count as 0.0; CR/NC/P/NP/W/IP/MG/IN do not affect GPA. Transfer GPA and Gould Law grading are separate. Repeat Impact is disabled because freshman grade substitution has eligibility rules.
helpExample: A 4-unit A earns 16.0 grade points and a 4-unit B+ earns 13.2. Together, 29.2 ÷ 8 = 3.650.

gradeExplanations.F: F counts as zero grade points.
gradeExplanations.UW: Unofficial withdrawal counts as zero grade points.
gradeExplanations.IX: Expired incomplete counts as zero grade points.
gradeExplanations.CR: Credit; no effect on USC GPA.
gradeExplanations.NC: No Credit; no effect on USC GPA.
gradeExplanations.P: Pass; no effect on USC GPA.
gradeExplanations.NP: No Pass; no effect on USC GPA.
gradeExplanations.W: Withdrawal; no effect on USC GPA.
gradeExplanations.MG: Missing Grade; excluded while unresolved; if unresolved for one year it becomes UW.
gradeExplanations.IN: Incomplete; excluded while unresolved; if it expires it normally becomes IX.

specialTypes.name: USC course, standard grading
specialTypes.note: Use final USC transcript grade and semester units.

specialTypes.name: Verified freshman-forgiveness original attempt
specialTypes.note: Use only after confirming the course qualifies for USC freshman grade substitution; the replacement grade should be entered separately as a standard USC course.

specialTypes.name: External transfer course
specialTypes.note: Transfer grades are kept separate from the USC institutional GPA. Graduation/honors may also consider a combined USC-transfer GPA.

specialTypes.name: Gould Law course / law record
specialTypes.note: Gould Law uses a more granular grading system. Do not apply the ordinary USC undergraduate mapping without record-specific review.

repeatPolicy.note: Repeat Impact is disabled because USC repeat treatment depends on freshman status, timing, grade, and substitution eligibility. Use the special course type only after confirming freshman-forgiveness eligibility.
